title: Inventory reservations over HTTP
prompt: Build an in-memory HTTP inventory service. All bodies are JSON. SKUs match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}. PUT /items/:sku with body exactly {stock} (integer 0..1000000000) creates an item and returns 201 {sku,available}; an existing item returns 409; a bad SKU, body or stock returns 400. GET /items/:sku returns 200 {sku,available} or 404. POST /items/:sku/reserve requires an Idempotency-Key header (1..64 characters, otherwise 400) and a body exactly {quantity} (integer 1..1000, otherwise 400). Check in this order: 400 for header/body problems, 404 for an unknown SKU, replay handling, then stock. A key seen before with the same SKU and quantity replays the original 201 response body exactly and changes nothing; a key seen before with a different SKU or quantity returns 422. A new key reserves the quantity: when available is at least quantity it returns 201 {reservation_id,sku,quantity,status:"active"} and reduces available; otherwise it returns 409 and nothing is recorded, so the same key may be used again later. Reservation IDs are unique nonempty strings. Idempotency keys are global across SKUs. POST /reservations/:id/release returns 200 {reservation_id,sku,quantity,status:"released"} and returns the quantity to available on the first call; repeating it returns the same 200 body and changes nothing; an unknown ID returns 404. Available stock must never go below zero, even for concurrent requests. No persistence or external services are needed.
